To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) schooling and work experience are important determinants of wage growth, (2) chronological age is not a significant determinant of wage growth, and (3) the effect of schooling and experience on wage growth is not significantly different across age groups.
(a) the effect of chronological aging is negative; (b) the effect of job experience on wage growth is positive and (c) the effect of schooling on wage growth is also positive.
(1) the wage growth rate declines with age, and (2) the effect of chronological aging on wage growth is negative.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of schooling, experience, and age on wage growth.
the following questions: What is the effect of schooling and experience on wages?
the following question: How does the growth in the wage of a young male worker depend upon changes in his schooling, job experience, and age?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for men aged 18-34, the wage growth is largely explained by the growth of experience and education, and the negative effect of aging per se is negligible.
the effects of aging, experience and schooling on wage growth are complex and not fully understood.
the effect of chronological aging on wages is small, but that it is negative.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
wage growth is primarily due to changes in job experience.
the wage-age profile is a combination of the effects of schooling, experience, and chronological age.
schooling and experience are important determinants of wage growth and aging has little effect on wage growth.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is important to distinguish between the effect of aging and other changes that occur over time, such as changes in job experience or schooling.
the effect of aging per se is small relative to other factors, and that the effect of experience is large relative to other factors.
the effect of chronological aging is small and that it is important to control for the effects of schooling and experience in order to estimate the effects of age per se.
